domain: detection and repair of AI slop in prose, code, documentation, and agent output, grounded in corpus evidence rather than authorship detection
refresh_cadence: 30 days for model-specific marker cohorts and detector claims; 90 days for corpus studies and regulation; before every release for any numeric claim

researched_requires: at least two captured sources for fast-moving or high-stakes domains
at least one official/primary source for lower-risk domains
retrieved dates, refresh_due dates, source_type, confidence, and claim coverage
downgrade_rules: Vendor study with no methodology or sample size: cap confidence at low and tier at CONTESTED
Single-author unaffiliated preprint: cap confidence at medium and tier at CONTESTED
Marketing page with no date and no citation: tier FOLKLORE, never quoted as a measured figure
Preprint verified at abstract level only: cap tier at CONTESTED regardless of how strong the claim reads
Vendor selling a product the finding would sell more of: record the conflict in limitations
rules.operating_rule: Never attach a practitioner impact claim to an official vendor URL. The URL supports what the vendor said, not whether it is true.

sources.title: Measuring AI Slop in Text
claims: LLM-as-judge agreement with human slop labels is near zero: GPT-5 kappa 0.01, DeepSeek-V3 kappa -0.01, o3-mini kappa 0.03
Models flag slop at a 0.03 to 0.08 rate versus humans at 0.34, under-flagging by roughly five times
Span-level slop extraction by GPT-5 runs at precision 0.14 and recall 0.11; a fine-tuned Qwen-7B reaches 0.32 and 0.30
sources.limitations: Preprint, verified at abstract level. Revision date 2026-01-24.
sources.methodology: LLM judges evaluated against human slop annotations on a labelled corpus.

sources.title: AI-AI bias: large language models favor communications generated by large language models
claims: GPT-4 preferred LLM-written product pitches 89 percent of the time versus human raters at 36 percent
The same direction appears for papers at 78 versus 61 percent and movies at 70 versus 58 percent
The p below 10 to the minus 16 figures describe LLM selectors preferring LLM text over human text in the product and movie experiments; the papers experiment is at P equal to 0.001
sources.limitations: The human baseline is n equal to 13 in total, 6 per dataset, and the authors write that the findings are not definitive. That n must travel with any quotation of the human-versus-model preference gap. The reported p-values test whether LLM selectors prefer LLM text, NOT the human-rater-versus-LLM-rater gap the percentages describe. That gap has no significance test in the paper. Do not attach a p-value to it.

sources.title: Style Outweighs Substance: Failure Modes of LLM Judges in Alignment Benchmarking
claims: LLM judge preferences do not correlate with factuality or safety measures
sources.limitations: Verified at abstract level. The finding is that judge preference does not track factuality or safety on the benchmarks studied; it does not establish that judges are useless for every task, only that preference is not a proxy for correctness.

sources.title: Judging the Judges
claims: Judge style bias ranges from 0.10 to 0.76, with markdown preferred over plain text, against position bias of 0.04 or less
Verbosity bias is model-family specific: Gemini and Llama plus 0.24 to plus 0.44, Claude minus 0.12, GPT-4o minus 0.04
sources.limitations: TMLR 2026 acceptance stated; verified at abstract level.

sources.title: Limits to scalable evaluation at the frontier
claims: When the judge is no more accurate than the model it evaluates, no debiasing method can reduce required ground-truth labels by more than half
sources.limitations: A theoretical result with stated assumptions, not an empirical measurement. The bound applies when the judge is no more accurate than the evaluated model. It does not forbid useful evaluation by a genuinely stronger judge or by ground truth.

sources.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
claims: Self-recognition ability correlates linearly with self-preference strength, argued to be causal
sources.limitations: Verified at abstract level. The causal claim between self-recognition and self-preference is argued by the authors rather than established by intervention, and the effect is measured on a limited model set.

sources.title: When AI Reviews Its Own Code: Recursive Self-Training Collapse in Code LLMs
claims: AI self-review gates enter a rubber-stamp regime where acceptance scores rise while benchmark correctness falls
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level only.
sources.title_correction_note: Title corrected 2026-07-28 after independent arXiv resolution. The ledger previously carried the descriptive placeholder "Recursive collapse in AI self-review gates for code", which resolved to no paper. The identifier was always correct; the title was not.

sources.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
claims: At least 13.5 percent of 2024 PubMed abstracts were processed with an LLM, reaching 40 percent in some subcorpora
Excess words are overwhelmingly stylistic verbs and adjectives rather than content words
The method is detector-free, comparing observed against extrapolated word frequencies
sources.limitations: The widely quoted 10 percent and 30 percent figures come from the superseded June 2024 preprint version and must not be used. The preprint at arXiv 2406.07016 has five live versions and carries no withdrawal notice, so it was revised rather than withdrawn; describing it as withdrawn would itself be a citation defect.
sources.methodology: Over 15 million PubMed abstracts, 2010 to 2024. Peer reviewed, Science Advances 11(27), DOI 10.1126/sciadv.adt3813.
sources.source_date_note: Crossref reports the publication date as 2025-07-04 while this ledger records 2025-07-02. Most likely an online-first versus issue date difference, but that was not confirmed. Both dates are recorded rather than one being silently overwritten. Crossref independently confirms the title, journal, volume 11 and issue 27; science.org returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch, which is a publisher block rather than non-resolution.

sources.title: Em-ergence of the em-dash
claims: Em-dash prevalence in medRxiv Discussion sections rose from 4.23 percent pre-ChatGPT to 11.58 percent post, a 7.35 point rise with 95 percent CI 6.94 to 7.77 and odds ratio 2.96
The trajectory runs at about 4 percent through 2023, 8.0 percent in 2024, and 20.3 percent in 2025
A placebo split within the pre-LLM era showed no change, plus 0.13 points
The author concludes the em-dash is a population-level indicator, not a per-paper detector of LLM use
sources.methodology: Pre-registered on OSF as HFT8C. 69,632 medRxiv preprints.
sources.limitations: Preprint. Pre-registration substantially raises confidence relative to unregistered vendor claims.

sources.title: Pangram supporting evidence page
claims: The page claims humans average 5 em dashes per 10,000 words while model families range from 3 to 45
The page separately claims a human figure of 2 against AI 17 in its summary table, contradicting its own by-model section
The page claims AI uses tricolons about four times as often as humans
sources.limitations: No sample size, no corpus description, no methodology, no citation, and no date. States two different human baselines on the same page. Contradicted by the independently measured baseline in the Freeburg preprint. Recorded so the brain can explain why it is not used; never quoted as a measured figure.

sources.title: The Last Fingerprint: How Markdown Training Shapes LLM Prose
claims: Measured human em-dash baseline of 3.23 per 1,000 words, equal to 32.3 per 10,000
Em-dash rate is a signature of a specific fine-tuning procedure rather than a universal AI tell
RLHF can eliminate the marker as well as amplify it: base Llama 3.1 8B at 0.49 per 1,000 versus instruction-tuned at 0.00
sources.limitations: Single-author, unaffiliated, non-peer-reviewed preprint. Must not be cited alongside peer-reviewed work without this flag.

sources.title: Saying More Than They Know
claims: LLMs produce tricolons at nearly twice the expert human rate
LLMs produce hesitancy markers at roughly twice human density
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level.

sources.title: The Rise of Verbal Tics in LLMs
claims: Verbal Tic Index across eight frontier models: Gemini 3.1 Pro 0.590 worst, GPT-5.4 0.411, Claude Opus 4.7 0.317, DeepSeek V3.2 0.295 best
Human evaluation with n equal to 120 found a correlation of minus 0.87 between sycophancy and perceived naturalness
Top tics include Absolutely, That's a great question, It's important to note, and delve
sources.limitations: Preprint. The model roster differs between versions, so per-model numbers are cohort-specific and will rot.

sources.title: Idiosyncrasies in Large Language Models
claims: Five-way model attribution reaches 97.1 percent accuracy across ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, and DeepSeek
The signal survives rewriting, translation, and summarization
sources.limitations: High attribution accuracy is a capability result, not a licence to attribute. This brain cites it only to explain why fingerprinting is refused. Model rosters age quickly, so the 97.1 percent figure is cohort-specific and will not hold for models released after the study.

sources.title: StoryScope
claims: 93.2 percent macro-F1 separating human from AI stories using narrative and discourse features alone
68.4 percent accuracy on six-way model attribution
The Claude signature is notably flat event escalation
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level.

sources.title: Voice Under Revision
claims: LLM revision decreases function words, contractions, and first-person pronouns while increasing vocabulary diversity and word length
The shift persists even under explicit instructions to preserve the author's voice
Rewritten texts converge in feature space regardless of their starting point
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level.

sources.title: People who frequently use ChatGPT for writing tasks are accurate and robust detectors of AI-generated text
claims: A majority vote of five expert annotators misclassified only 1 of 300 articles
Expert humans outperformed commercial and open-source detectors even under paraphrase evasion
sources.limitations: The annotators were self-selected frequent LLM users, so the result describes what experienced humans can do rather than what an average reviewer will do. One error in 300 is a majority-vote figure across five annotators; individual accuracy is lower, and the cost of five expert reviews is the practical constraint.

sources.title: Identifying Bias in Machine-generated Text Detection
claims: English-language-learner essays are more likely to be flagged by machine-generated text detectors
Non-White ELL students were disproportionately flagged relative to White ELL peers
Human annotators showed no significant demographic bias on the same essays
sources.methodology: 16 detection models on student essays labelled for gender, race and ethnicity, ELL status, and socioeconomic status. Published at ACL 2026 by Pindrop researchers.
sources.limitations: Supersedes the 2023 Liang finding as the current peer-reviewed citation for detector demographic bias.

sources.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
claims: Seven detectors misclassified 61.3 percent of TOEFL essays as AI-generated
19.8 percent of those essays were unanimously flagged by all detectors
sources.methodology: Patterns 4(7):100779. Seven detectors on 91 TOEFL essays.
sources.limitations: The n equals 91 sample size must be stated whenever the 61.3 percent figure is quoted. Essays predate 2020. Superseded for currency by Stowe et al. ACL 2026.

sources.title: New AI classifier for indicating AI-written text
claims: OpenAI's own classifier identified 26 percent of AI-written text as likely AI-written
It incorrectly labelled human-written text as AI-written 9 percent of the time
OpenAI withdrew the classifier on 2023-07-20 due to its low rate of accuracy
sources.limitations: The OpenAI page returns 403 to automated fetch. Figures confirmed through Search Engine Land and The Register coverage of the withdrawal note.

sources.title: DAMAGE: Detecting Adversarially Modified AI Generated Text
claims: All humanizers tend to degrade the quality of the original text
Fluency win rate of humanized text against the original was 26.0 percent for best-tier tools, 14.67 percent medium, 2.67 percent worst
Documented failure modes include hallucinated citations, comment leakage, and nonsensical strings
SynthID-Text true positive rate at 5 percent false positive rate falls from 87.6 percent to 5.4 percent after DIPPER paraphrase
sources.limitations: Authored by Pangram employees, who sell a detector. The finding that humanizers evade detection serves their commercial interest; the finding that humanizers degrade quality does not, which raises confidence in the latter.

sources.title: Base Models Look Human To AI Detectors
claims: Llama3-8B base model output was rated 98.8 percent human by Pangram
The authors conclude that detectors capture artifacts of instruction tuning rather than machine generation
Iterative paraphrasing reaches 100 percent human probability by round 10 while semantic preservation collapses from 99 to 100 down to a 33 to 99 range
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level.

sources.title: Wikipedia:Signs of AI writing
claims: The guide states the listed patterns are only potential signs of a problem, not the problem itself
It warns explicitly not to merely treat the signs as the problems to be fixed, because that could just make detection harder
It documents a markup taxonomy of vendor residue markers including oaicite, bracketed cite tokens, grok-card, and utm_source tracking parameters
It documents a citations taxonomy covering fabricated references, invalid DOIs and ISBNs, and DOIs pointing at unrelated papers
It maintains an ineffective-indicators list of signals that should not be treated as evidence
It notes that AI vocabulary shifts by model era and gives dated cohorts
sources.limitations: A living community guide, descriptive rather than prescriptive. Snapshot captured 2026-07-27; the page changes continuously.

sources.title: Wikipedia:Writing articles with large language models RfC close
claims: The RfC closed 2026-03-20 by a 44 to 2 margin under SNOW
It prohibits using LLMs to generate or rewrite article content
Two exceptions survive: copyediting your own writing, and LLM-assisted translation, both under mandatory human review
It is a content guideline, not a policy
sources.limitations: Commonly mis-described as a policy. The distinction matters when citing it as authority.

sources.title: blader/humanizer agent skill
claims: Version 2.9.1 as of 2026-07-22, MIT licensed, 31,520 stars and 2,879 forks at retrieval
It enumerates 33 patterns derived from the Wikipedia signs guide
It has no severity system, no confidence system, and no per-pattern weights
Its no-fabrication rule is a prompt instruction with no verification mechanism
It has no coverage of fabricated citations, vendor residue markers, or code
Its section 14 bans en dashes outright, which breaks legitimate numeric and date ranges
Its own runtime prompt contains an em dash, violating its own stated hard constraint
sources.limitations: Repository state changes continuously; snapshot taken 2026-07-27. Star count is a moving figure and must be re-checked before quoting.

sources.title: We Have a Package for You! A Comprehensive Analysis of Package Hallucinations by Code Generating LLMs
claims: 19.7 percent of packages recommended by code LLMs did not exist, averaged across 16 models and 576,000 samples
205,474 unique hallucinated package names were observed
Commercial models hallucinated at 5.2 percent against 21.7 percent for open-source models
43 percent of hallucinations recurred across all ten reruns of the same prompt and 58 percent recurred more than once
sources.limitations: Model cohort is from 2024. See the Churilov source for current rates before quoting the 19.7 percent figure as current.

sources.title: The Range Shrinks, the Threat Remains: Re-evaluating LLM Package Hallucinations on the 2026 Frontier-Model Cohort
claims: 2026 frontier models hallucinate packages at 4.62 percent to 6.10 percent, an order of magnitude compression from the 2024 cohort spread
Claude Haiku 4.5 measured 4.62 percent and GPT-5.4-mini measured 6.10 percent
53 hallucinated package names remained registerable at time of measurement
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level.
sources.title_correction_note: Title corrected 2026-07-28 after independent arXiv resolution. The ledger previously carried the descriptive placeholder "Package hallucination rates in 2026 frontier models", which resolved to no paper. The identifier was always correct; the title was not.

sources.title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
claims: Allowing AI increased task completion time by 19 percent for experienced developers on mature repositories
Developers forecast a 24 percent speedup and still estimated a 20 percent speedup after the fact
Economists forecast a 39 percent speedup and machine learning experts 38 percent
sources.methodology: Randomized controlled trial, 16 developers, 246 real tasks.
sources.limitations: Small n. METR's own 2026-02-24 follow-up could not obtain a clean signal because developers increasingly refused to work without AI.

sources.title: Echoes of AI: Investigating the Downstream Effects of AI Assistants on Software Maintainability
claims: Phase 2 found no significant differences in subsequent code evolution, completion time, or quality between AI-assisted and unassisted development
Phase 1, observational, found a 30.7 percent median reduction in completion time with an AI assistant, and an estimated 55.9 percent speedup for habitual AI users
The study was preregistered with In-Principle Acceptance before data collection
sources.methodology: 151 participants. Preprint at arXiv 2507.00788, pre-registered with In-Principle Acceptance granted at ICSME. It carries no journal reference and is not a published paper.
sources.limitations: PREPRINT, not published. The arXiv comment reads "Preprint of study preregistered at ICSME 2025 with In-Principal Acceptance", and the In-Principle Acceptance was granted at the 40th ICSME in 2024. It has no journal reference. The null result is Phase 2 only. Phase 1 of the same study was observational and found the opposite direction: a 30.7 percent median reduction in completion time using an AI assistant, and an estimated 55.9 percent speedup for habitual AI users. Any citation of this source that reports only the null is incomplete.
sources.title_correction_note: Title corrected 2026-07-28 after independent arXiv resolution. The ledger previously carried the descriptive placeholder "Does Co-Development with AI Assistants Lead to More Maintainable Code?", which resolved to no paper. The identifier was always correct; the title was not.

sources.title: The AI Code Quality Maintainability Gap
claims: Block duplication climbed from 40.3 per million changed lines in 2023 to 73.0 in 2026 year to date, a rise of 81 percent
The 2026 report measures two-week code churn at plus 15 percent rather than reporting a churn level
sources.limitations: Correlational, not causal. GitClear sells code-quality tooling, so the finding serves its commercial interest. The often-quoted 7.1 percent churn figure is a discarded 2024 projection, never an actual measurement; the 2024 actual was 5.7 percent.

sources.title: AI Copilot Code Quality 2025
claims: Moved or refactored code fell from 24.8 percent in 2021 to 9.5 percent in 2024
Copy-pasted code rose from 8.3 percent to 12.3 percent over the same period
There was an eight-fold increase in code blocks containing five or more duplicated lines during 2024
Code churn was 3.1 percent in 2020, 3.3 percent in 2021 and 2022, 4.5 percent in 2023, projected 7.1 percent for 2024 and actually 5.7 percent
sources.limitations: Vendor-produced and correlational.

sources.title: High-Quality Chaos
claims: The curl maintainer states the slop situation is not a problem anymore
Report frequency runs at about double the rate seen through 2025
The confirmed-vulnerability rate returned to 15 to 16 percent
curl returned to HackerOne on 2026-03-01 without a bounty
sources.limitations: First-hand maintainer account, not a controlled study. Directly contradicts the common narrative that curl abandoned bug bounties permanently.

sources.title: AI-Generated Workslop Is Destroying Productivity
claims: 40 percent of United States desk workers received workslop in the prior month
Each incident took roughly two hours to resolve
The estimated cost is 186 dollars per employee per month, or about 9 million dollars a year at 10,000 employees
Roughly 15 percent of received content qualified as workslop
sources.methodology: BetterUp Labs with Stanford Social Media Lab, n equals 1,150 United States desk workers, fielded September 2025. Published in Harvard Business Review 2025-09-22.
sources.limitations: Self-reported survey estimates, not controlled measurement. The Harvard Business Review article body is paywalled; figures confirmed on BetterUp's own page.

sources.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data
claims: Recursive training on generated data causes early collapse where distribution tails and variance are lost, and late collapse where the model converges to a low-variance point estimate
The effect was demonstrated on Gaussian mixture models, variational autoencoders, and OPT language models
sources.limitations: An Author Correction exists, Nature s41586-025-08905-3, whose scope could not be read behind the publisher auth wall. The collapse result assumes data replacement; the accumulation literature argues collapse is largely avoided when synthetic data accumulates alongside human data with curation.

sources.title: Slop is the new name for unwanted AI-generated content
claims: The canonical definition is behavioural: not all AI-generated content is slop, but if it is mindlessly generated and thrust upon someone who did not ask for it, slop is the perfect term for it
Willison proposed slom for the AI-generated subset of spam in a 2024-05-09 update
sources.limitations: An influential essay, not a study. Cited for the definition it established, not for any empirical claim.

sources.title: Merriam-Webster 2025 Word of the Year: slop
claims: Merriam-Webster defines slop as digital content of low quality that is produced usually in quantity by means of artificial intelligence
Runners-up were gerrymander, performative, touch grass, six seven, and Lake Chargoggagoggmanchauggagoggchaubunagungamaugg
The American Dialect Society also selected slop, voting 2026-01-09
sources.limitations: merriam-webster.com is Cloudflare-blocked to automated fetch, so the announcement was verified through the GlobeNewswire press release wire copy dated 2025-12-15. The frequently repeated claim that tariff was a runner-up is false.

sources.title: EU AI Act Article 50 transparency obligations
claims: Article 50 transparency duties apply from 2026-08-02 and were not amended by the Digital Omnibus
The Digital Omnibus, adopted by Parliament 2026-06-16 and Council 2026-06-29, deferred high-risk deadlines only
Generative systems already on the market before 2026-08-02 have until 2026-12-02 for the Article 50(2) machine-readable marking requirement
Penalties reach 15 million euro or 3 percent of turnover
sources.limitations: A consolidated third-party rendering of the regulation rather than the Official Journal text. Verify against EUR-Lex before relying on it for compliance advice.

sources.title: Verifying Provenance of Digital Media: Why the C2PA Specifications Fall Short
claims: The analysis concludes the C2PA specifications fail to achieve their claimed security goals
It states the specifications should not yet be relied upon for high-stakes uses such as financial disclosures, journalism, or legal evidence
It finds that specification version 2.4 does not address the identified problems
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level. Claims that C2PA is now ISO/IEC 22144 could not be verified against any primary source and appear only in marketing material.
sources.title_correction_note: Title corrected 2026-07-28 after independent arXiv resolution. The ledger previously carried the descriptive placeholder "Independent security analysis of the C2PA specifications", which resolved to no paper. The identifier was always correct; the title was not.

sources.title: ELEPHANT: measuring social sycophancy in language models
claims: Language models preserve user face 45 percentage points more than humans do
Models affirm both sides in 48 percent of moral conflicts
sources.limitations: Publication date precision is year only, pending confirmation of the issue date.

sources.title: Anthropic study of sycophancy in production conversations
claims: 9 percent of guidance conversations were sycophantic overall
The rate was 25 percent for relationships and 38 percent for spirituality
Opus 4.7 showed roughly half the sycophancy rate of Opus 4.6
sources.limitations: First-party vendor research about the vendor's own models. No published study counts the specific phrase You're absolutely right in coding-agent transcripts.

sources.title: Empirical evidence of Large Language Model's influence on human spoken communication
claims: Words preferentially generated by ChatGPT increased abruptly in spontaneous human speech
Delve usage rose 48 percent, realm 35 percent, and adept 51 percent within 18 months of ChatGPT's release
A preregistered experiment with n equal to 496 confirmed entrenchment in active vocabulary
sources.methodology: Over 740,000 hours across 824,634 podcast episodes and 20,000 academic YouTube channels.
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level. Causation between model output and human speech is inferred for the corpus portion, not experimentally isolated.

sources.title: What Are LLMs Doing to Scientific Communication? Measuring Changes in Writing Practices and Reading Experience
claims: LLM-modified text shows lower lexical diversity than unmodified text
Domain experts rated LLM-improved texts as more understandable and more exciting
The same experts expressed negative qualitative attitudes towards LLMs, so the quantitative rating and the stated attitude point in opposite directions
sources.limitations: Preprint verified at abstract level. Directly complicates the premise that slop is self-evidently worse writing.
sources.title_correction_note: Title corrected 2026-07-28 after independent arXiv resolution. The ledger previously carried the descriptive placeholder "Lexical diversity and reader response in LLM-modified academic text", which resolved to no paper. The identifier was always correct; the title was not.

sources.title: From Industry Claims to Empirical Reality: An Empirical Study of Code Review Agents in Pull Requests
claims: Pull requests handled only by code review agents achieve a 45.20 percent merge rate, 23.17 percentage points lower than human-only pull requests at 68.37 percent
60.2 percent of closed agent-only pull requests fall into the 0 to 30 percent signal range
sources.methodology: Accepted at the 23rd International Conference on Mining Software Repositories, MSR 2026. Authors Kowshik Chowdhury, Dipayan Banik, K M Ferdous, Shazibul Islam Shamim.
sources.limitations: Previously blocked from this ledger because an earlier research pass recorded the wrong arXiv identifier, 2603.28592, which is Liu et al. on technical debt. The correct identifier is 2604.03196, resolved 2026-07-28. Accepted at MSR 2026; verified at abstract level.
